suggestion: Publish a one-line rights status at the top of every page (licensed / unlicensed / unknown) and stop the build if a page renders a price without one.
problem_it_solves: The whole pack is built on NFL data whose Terms §1.3 restrict non-informational and systematic use; a reader currently has to hunt for that.
risk_if_adopted: A missing tag would silently allow an unlicensed price onto a page, so the checker must fail closed.
decision_owner_needs: A decision on which licence, if any, will be obtained.

suggestion: Give every table cell exactly one of four states: verified, computed, blank-unverified, blocked. Never let a computed number look like an official one.
problem_it_solves: Readers cannot tell whether 'own_total 43.86' is an NFL figure or our arithmetic. It is our arithmetic.
risk_if_adopted: Three or four states invite argument at the boundary; the definitions must be written down once.

suggestion: Stamp every page with the read time of the underlying source and a SHA-256 of each input CSV.
problem_it_solves: A table with no timestamp cannot be audited; a reader cannot tell a 2-minute-old snapshot from a 2-month-old one.
risk_if_adopted: Hashes must be regenerated on every build or the manifest lies.

suggestion: Add a 'Decision needed' column to the suggestions table and leave it empty until the owner answers. Never pre-fill it.
problem_it_solves: Suggestions currently read as recommendations; the brief asks for a place to review and *choose*.
risk_if_adopted: An empty column looks unfinished unless the page explains that the blank is the point.

suggestion: Print a confidence interval beside every aggregate that has one, and print 'no interval available' where it does not.
problem_it_solves: Point estimates without intervals invite over-reading, which is the exact failure the brief warns about.
risk_if_adopted: Intervals on dependent observations (weeks, clubs) will be too narrow unless clustered; an unclustered interval is worse than none.
decision_owner_needs: A decision on the clustering unit (game, week, or season).

suggestion: Request a dated depth-chart feed. Every club chart read says 'unofficial' and none carries a publication time.
problem_it_solves: The deficiency analysis cannot say when a chart was correct, so a 'starter' could already have been replaced.
risk_if_adopted: A dated feed costs money and may not exist for all 32 clubs.

suggestion: Capture the injury page and the inactive list with an HTTP Date header and a hash, on a schedule, not by hand.
problem_it_solves: The brief forbids manual input; a hand-read page cannot prove when it was read.
risk_if_adopted: A scheduled scraper conflicts with NFL Terms §1.3 unless licensed.
decision_owner_needs: A licence that permits automated retrieval.

suggestion: Show the model's formula, its inputs and its omissions on the same page as its output (no home-field term, no opponent adjustment).
problem_it_solves: An own line that silently omits home field looks more precise than it is.
risk_if_adopted: Publishing the formula invites imitation; that is acceptable here.

suggestion: Keep the qualified board and a clearly labelled provisional board separate, and never sort them together.
problem_it_solves: An unqualified hypothesis sitting next to a qualified strategy reads as a ranking.
risk_if_adopted: Two boards double the maintenance and can confuse a casual reader.
decision_owner_needs: Owner decision on whether a provisional board may exist at all.

suggestion: Publish the luck-vs-skill test *before* any results, with the threshold fixed in git, so the test cannot be chosen after seeing the data.
problem_it_solves: Any test picked after the fact is a licence to find 'skill' in noise.
risk_if_adopted: A pre-registered test may fail and embarrass the project; that is the point.

suggestion: Register the *sign* of each dependence before measuring it, and treat a sign error as a failed gate.
problem_it_solves: A correlation computed after seeing the data can always be explained.
risk_if_adopted: Some pairs will turn out to have no measurable dependence, which invalidates the combo built on them.

suggestion: Commit the input manifest (SHA-256 per CSV) so a reviewer can prove the page came from the file.
problem_it_solves: Without it, a table and a CSV can drift apart silently.
risk_if_adopted: Hashes change on every input edit, so the manifest must be rebuilt, not hand-edited.

suggestion: Follow nfl.com's own week label everywhere and cite the schedule URL as proof.
problem_it_solves: External sources number the same slate differently, which would mislabel every row.
risk_if_adopted: A single numbering scheme will still disagree with some third-party sites.

suggestion: One shared navigation strip generated from a single list for every page in the repo.
problem_it_solves: Each dashboard is hand-maintained, so sections drift and a reader cannot tell which is current.
risk_if_adopted: A shared nav touches every page; one bad edit breaks all of them, and other sessions own those pages.
decision_owner_needs: Agreement from every session that owns a page (shared output).

suggestion: Add a glossary panel defining every status label (Out/Doubtful/Questionable, Full/Limited/DNP, 1st/2nd/3rd/4th string) with the official definition and a link.
problem_it_solves: The page uses official labels whose meaning is not obvious and whose probabilities are not published.
risk_if_adopted: A glossary can drift from the policy if the policy changes.

suggestion: Make every wide table scroll horizontally with a frozen first column instead of shrinking the font.
problem_it_solves: Wide evidence tables become unreadable on a phone, which is where most review happens.
risk_if_adopted: Frozen columns need CSS care across browsers.

suggestion: Show, on the dashboard, the count of blank cells and the count of blocked gates, and refuse to hide them behind a summary.
problem_it_solves: Blank cells are the most informative thing on the page and are easy to sweep away.
risk_if_adopted: A large blank count may look like failure; it is the honest state.

suggestion: Publish a one-command reproduction (`python3 scripts/build_nfl_wk.py && python3 scripts/check_nfl_wk.py`) and require it in CI.
problem_it_solves: A reader cannot currently regenerate the tables, so errors cannot be isolated.
risk_if_adopted: CI minutes and a hard failure mode if the build is not deterministic.

suggestion: Keep the NFL pack in its own directory and link it from the shared index rather than merging it into an existing dashboard.
problem_it_solves: Concurrent sessions edit the same shared pages; merging would cause conflicting edits.
risk_if_adopted: A separate directory can stagnate if nobody links it.
decision_owner_needs: Final integration decision on the site's information architecture.
